det.desc: DESCRIPTION: 1954 TOULOUSE-LAUTREC “OEUVRE GRAPHIQUE” — GALERIE DES PONCHETTES, NICE — MOURLOT LITHOGRAPHIC EXHIBITION POSTER An especially interesting piece from this collection: the 1954 lithographic exhibition poster for Oeuvre graphique de Toulouse-Lautrec at the Galerie des Ponchettes in Nice, France. The exhibition was held from January 30 through March 15, 1954 at Galerie des Ponchettes, 77 Quai des États-Unis, Nice, and was devoted to Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec’s graphic work. The official City of Nice heritage record identifies the exhibition poster as a 1954 production by Mourlot in Paris. This particular example was purchased at the exhibition itself in 1954 and has remained with the same six-piece group of Toulouse-Lautrec lithographs acquired there. THE IMAGE The poster incorporates Toulouse-Lautrec’s imagery from Au Moulin Rouge, featuring La Goulue and her sister, together with the exhibition typography and information for the Galerie des Ponchettes. Rather than simply reproducing one of Lautrec’s commercial posters, this sheet was specifically created to announce the 1954 Nice retrospective, making it an artifact of the exhibition itself. rows.t: Mid-century Brass Rooster

det.desc: Decorative brass animal figurines gained immense popularity during the mid-20th century, particularly within Hollywood Regency and transitional interior design schemes. Artisans often utilized lost-wax or sand-casting techniques to achieve highly textured surfaces that caught the light and added dramatic flair to home decor. Roosters, symbolizing vigilance and courage, were frequently cast as paired fighting or strutting display pieces for dining rooms and entryways. Many of these expressive brass sculptures were produced in European foundries, notably in Italy and parts of Spain, before being exported to American department stores and interior design boutiques. The rich patinas and meticulous feather detailing reflect a period when heavy, sculptural brass accessories were a hallmark of sophisticated interior styling. Over the decades, these charming decorative animals have transitioned from mainstream home furnishings into sought-after vintage collectibles. 11” at tallest 6 1/2” at widest

rows.t: Murano Blue & White Art Glass Vase Ruffled Rim Clear Star Base

det.desc: Murano glass has a rich heritage rooted in the Venetian lagoon island of San Murano, where the art of glassmaking was concentrated starting in the late 13th century to prevent fires in Venice. Master artisans passed down secret techniques through generations, perfecting methods like cased glass, where multiple layers of colored glass are fused together. The iconic trumpet or Jack-in-the-Pulpit silhouette became exceptionally popular during the mid-20th century as modern interior design embraced dramatic, organic forms and vibrant color palettes. Techniques such as rigati or optic ribbing and contrasting rim applications showcase the high level of skill required by Venetian gaffers working at the furnace. Mid-century Italian glass factories exported these decorative pieces worldwide, making them prized centerpieces in homes adopting eclectic or atomic-era aesthetics. Today, these distinctive pieces continue to be celebrated for their luminous colors and master craftsmanship. 9” tall 5 3/4” wide at widest point

rows.t: Kaoru Kawano (Japanese) Woodblock Print, Child In Foliage, Seal, Mid-Century

det.desc: Condition: Used, vintage. Framed woodblock print with wear consistent with age. See photos and notes below. Description: Original Japanese woodblock print by Kaoru Kawano (1916 to 1965), a leading artist of the sosaku hanga (creative print) movement, known for his simplified figures of children and animals and his use of visible wood grain as part of the design. This print depicts a young child curled among deep green and black foliage, the figure in warm ochre against a mottled woodgrain ground. It carries Kawano's carved red artist's seal in the lower right of the image. A white mineral ground (gofun) gives the surface its subtle sparkle, typical of his work. Kawano combined Western design with traditional Japanese woodblock technique and gained an international reputation through solo exhibitions in North America during the 1950s. Markings: Artist's red seal present in the image. No pencil signature or edition number is visible while matted, consistent with an open-edition strike. det.desc: Pair Vintage Antique Framed Hand Colored Engravings of Bald Eagle and Red Headed Woodpecker Engraved by W.H. Lizars, Edinburgh. William Home Lizars (1788–1859) was a leading Edinburgh engraver. From 1819 onward he produced plates for a number of natural history works, including Selby's Illustrations of British Ornithology , and his studio engraved and colored the plates for Jardine and Selby's Illustrations of Ornithology (1826–43). The obsolete Latin names match the 1820s–1840s period: Haliaetus leucocephalus for the bald eagle, and Picus erythrocephalus for the red-headed woodpecker, which was later reclassified as Melanerpes . The single birds on plain grounds and the lettering style fit Edinburgh natural-history plates of the 1830s. Edinburgh editions of Alexander Wilson's American Ornithology are the most likely source. rows.t: Vintage Faux Wood Grain Ceramic Foo Dog Figurine Seated Lion Pekingese Yongzheng

det.desc: For your consideration is this charming vintage mid-century Chinese export ceramic Foo Dog (Pekingese / Guardian Lion) figurine. This whimsical piece features an upward-gazing expression modeled after imperial Pekingese dogs, complete with a floppy ribbon collar holding a classic spherical crotal bell at its chest. The most striking element is its unique artistic finish: the ceramic body has been expertly glazed with swirling amber and dark brown lines to create a beautiful, highly convincing faux wood grain / carved burl wood illusion. The bottom features an iron-red double-square apocryphal reign stamp reading "雍正年製" (Yongzheng Nian Zhi), typical of late mid-century production workshops paying homage to earlier imperial eras. The piece also includes functional, original ventilation holes under the nostrils, mouth corners, and bell which allowed air to escape safely during kiln firing. A fantastic, eclectic addition to any Hollywood Regency, Asian-inspired, or mid-century maximalist home decor layout Apocryphal "Yongzheng Nian Zhi" Iron-Red Bottom Seal Stamp
